A. Present Annual Comprehensive Financial Report (ACFR) for Year Ended June 30, 2023
Recommended Action
Staff recommends that the City Council:
Receive and file the City’s Annual Comprehensive Financial Report (ACFR), the Auditors’ Letter to Council, and the Independent Auditors’ Report on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting and on Compliance and Other Matters Based on an Audit of Financial Statements Performed in Accordance with Government Auditing Standards for the City’s financial statements for the fiscal year ended June 30, 202 3 ; and
Adopt a finding of no significant effect pursuant to Section 15061(b)(3) (Common Sense Exemption) of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines .

B. Award a Contract for Aging and Disability Strategic Planning Consulting Services to Elizabeth Anderson Consulting
Recommended Action
Staff recommends that the City Council:
1. Adopt a finding of no possibility of significant effect pursuant to Section 15061(b)(3) (Common Sense Exemption) of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines;
2. Award RFP #400 to Elizabeth Anderson Consulting for consulting services in connection with establishing a citywide aging and disability strategic plan for the Housing and Human Services Department; and
3. Authorize the City Manager to negotiate and execute an agreement with Elizabeth Anderson Consulting in an amount not to exceed $155,000 for two years with future year funding contingent on Council budget approval .
Staff Report Printout

b. Attachment B: The Century Foundation - Economic Justice is Disability Justice

C. Award a Contract to Moss Adams, LLP for Human Services Grants Program Monitoring Services
Recommended Action
Staff recommends that the City Council:
1. Adopt a finding of no possibility of significant effect pursuant to Section 15061(b)(3) (Common Sense Exemption) of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines ;
2. Award RFP # 402 to Moss Adams, LLP, for ongoing compliance monitoring services for the H ousing and Human Services Department ; and
3. Authorize the City Manager to negotiate and execute an agreement with Moss Adams, LLP , for two years, with two additional one-year renewal options, for a total amoun t not to exceed $400,000 over a four year period, with future funding contingent on Council budget approval .

D. Approval of the Proposed FY 2024-25 Annual Action Plan Allocating Federal Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) and HOME Investment Partnerships Act Program (HOME) Entitlement Grant Funds
Recommended Action
Staff recommends that the City Council:
1. Adopt a finding of no possibility of significant effect pursuant to Section 15061(b)(3) (Common Sense Exemption) of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines.
2.               Approve the Proposed 2024-25 Annual Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) and HOME Action Plan (Attachment A).
3 . Authorize the City Manager to submit all documents required to receive the City’s annual CDBG and Home Investment Partnerships Act (HOME) entitlement grant funds to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD).

E. Approval of First Modification of Agreement #11250 with Steer for Rideshare Program Administration and Outreach
Recommended Action
Staff recommends that the City Council:
1. Adopt a finding of no possibility of significant effect pursuant to Section 15061(b)(3) (Common Sense Exemption) of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines ;
2. Authorize the City Manager to negotiate and execute a first modification to agreement #11250 in the amount of $96,200 with Steer , Inc. for rideshare program administration and outreach for the Department of Transportation , result ing in a three-year amended agreement (with two one-year optional extensions) with a new total amount not to exceed $1,497,698.48, with future year funding contingent on Council budget approval; and
3. Authorize budget amendment as outlined in the Financial Impacts and Budget Actions section of this report (requires 5 votes) .

F. Award Bid 4475 to California Waters Development, Inc. to Provide Water Feature and Pond Maintenance Citywide
R ecommended Action :
Staff recommends that the City Council:
1. Adopt a finding of categorical exemption pursuant to Section 15301 (Existing Facilities) of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines ;
2. Award Bid #4475 to California Waters Development, Inc. for the repair and maintenance of water features for the Public Works Department ; and
3. Authorize the City Manager to negotiate and execute an agreement with California Waters Development, Inc. for $1,285,596, plus a contingency of $186,429, for a two-year term, with three one-year renewal options , for a total amount not to exceed $1,472,025 over the five year period , with future year funding contingent on Council budget approval.

G. Approval to Accept U.S. Department of Energy's Energy Efficiency and Conservation Block Grant
Recommended Action
Staff recommends that the City Council:
1. Adopt a finding of no possibility of significant effect pursuant to Section 15061(b)(3) (Common Sense Exemption) of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines ;
2. Accept a grant awarded in the amount of $157,730 from the U.S. Department of Energy’s Energy Efficiency and Conservation Block Grant (EECBG) Program to fund an income-qualified electric bicycle (e-bike) voucher program in the Public Works Department, and to accept all grant renewals ;
3. Authori ze the City Manager to execute all necessary documents to accept the grant and all grant renewals ; and
4. Authorize budget amendment as outlined in the Financial Impacts & Budget Actions section of this report (requires 5 votes).
Staff Report Printout

H. Award Bid and Enter into Agreement with Flock Safety for Automatic License Plate Recognition (ALPR) cameras and Award Bid and Enter into Agreement with Constant Technologies for SMART Center Room Build-Out Services
Recommended Action
Staff recommends that the City Council:
1. Adopt a finding of no possibility of significant effect pursuant to Section 15061(b)(3) (Common Sense Exemption) of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines ;
2. Award RFP #394 to Flock Safety for the installation, leasing, maintenance, and support for 54 ALPR cameras for the Police Department ;
3. Award RFP #39 3 to Constant Technologies for the design, installation, and integration of video displays and workspace console s for the Santa Mo nica Analytical Real Time Center (SMART Center) for the Police Department ;
4. Authorize the City Manager to negotiate and execute an agreement with Flock Safety , for the leasing of 54 ALPR cameras in an amount not to exceed $494,100. This sum includes installation, maintenance, and support through December 3 1 , 2026, with future year funding contingent on Council Budget approval ; and
5. Authorize the City Manager to negotiate and execute an agreement with Constant Technologies, in an amount not to exceed $ 649 , 4 01 (including a $59,000 contingency) for a term of three years, with future year funding contingent on Council Budget approval.

I. Adoption of a Resolution that Amends Resolution No. 10325 (CCS) in order to Clarify the Authorization to Levy and Place the Main Street Business Area Festoon Lighting and Sidewalk Cleaning Assessments on the L.A. County Property Tax Rolls Each Year
Recommended Action
Staff recommends that the City Council :
1. Adopt a finding of n o possibility of significant effect pursuant to Section 15061(b)(3) (Common Sense Exemption) of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines.
2. Adopt a Resolution to amend Section 6 and Section 8 of Resolution No. 10325 (CCS) in order to clarify that Council authorized the levy and placement of the Main Street Business Area Festoon Lighting and Sidewalk Cleaning assessments on the Los Angeles County property tax rolls to be done annually and not just for FY 2008-2009.

A. Cannabis Social Equity Study Session
Recommended Action
Staff recommends that the City Council:
1. Review and discuss the presentation on cannabis social equity programs from other cities;
2. Provide direction on two potential policy options for approach to a cannabis social equity program within the City of Santa Monica which will determine the expansiveness of a social equity program and timeline by which staff returns with an ordinance; and
3. Discuss options and provide direction to staff on locational restrictions for the adult-use cannabis ordinance.

10. ORDINANCES
A. Introduction and First Reading of Low-Carbon Concrete Policy Ordinance and Adoption of Local Amendments Findings Resolution
R ecommended Action
Staff recommends that the City Council:
1. Adopt a finding of categorical exemption pursuant to Section 15308 of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines ;
2. Introduce for first reading the attached ordinance that adopts the 2022 California Green Building Standards Code including the 2022 intervening code updates , and supports decreasing emissions from concrete ;
3. Adopt the attached resolution that provides findings of local climatic, geological, topographical, and environme ntal conditions as required to adopt Santa Monica local amendments to the 2022 California Green Building Standards Code;
4. Direct the City Manager to file the adopted resolution and ordinance amending the Green Building Standards Code with the California Building Standards Commission following the second reading of the ordinance .

B. Introduction and First Reading of an Ordinance Amending the Text of the City's Zoning Ordinance to Update Provisions Related to State Density Bonus Law for Consistency with Recent Amendments to State law Adopted by AB 1287 and Making Other Minor Changes, Corrections, and Clarifications
Recommended Action
Staff recommends that the City Council:
1. Adopt a finding of no possibility of significant effect pursuant to Section 15061(b)(3) (Common Sense Exemption) of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines.
2. Introduce for First Reading of an Ordinance amending the text of the Zoning Ordinance to update provisions related to the implementation of State Density Bonus Law for consistency with recent amendments to State Law adopted by AB 1287 and make other minor changes, corrections, and clarifications.
3. Provide direction regarding the Planning Commission’s recommendation regarding a potential local density bonus program for projects that provide off-site affordable housing .

Request by Mayor Brock to direct the City Manager, City Attorney, and City Clerk to return with an amendment to the Council Rules to provide that Council 16 items may be handled like consent items, with the Council voting on them as one item, except for Council appointments to boards, commissions, and other bodies, and except for certain items that may be pulled for discussion at the Council meeting.
Staff Report Printout
C. Request of Councilmember de la Torre that the City Council allocate $5000 from its discretionary funds to the Association of Mexican American Educators in support of the Samohi Latino Graduation, organized by student group Legado Latino. These funds will assist in covering event expenses such as stoles, medals, diplomas, food and drinks, and entertainment. This event offers students a chance to celebrate their accomplishments and showcase their vibrant cultural heritage to the local community.
Staff Report Printout
a. Discretionary Funds as of 4.18.24
D. Request of Councilmember de la Torre that the City Council authorize use of existing travel funds to cover the costs (registration and travel expenses) of participating in the NALEO 41st Annual Conference, taking place June 18-20, 2024 in Las Vegas, NV. This annual conference provides an opportunity for Latino leaders from all across the country to network, exchange perspectives, and foster solutions around the most pressing policy issues affecting our communities today.
Staff Report Printout
a. Discretionary Funds as of 4.18.24
E. Request of Vice Mayor Negrete and Councilmember Parra that the City Council: 1) allocate up to $4681.72 from the Council Discretionary funds to cover costs associated with the rental of sound systems, a small stage, chairs, and related expenses for the Memorial Day event the Elks Lodge and American Legion Post are hosting at Woodlawn Cemetery in Santa Monica on May 27, 2024 to honor and pay tribute to those who have bravely fought to protect our nation, and 2) direct the City Manager to promote the event on the City’s social media platforms.
